newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore 1996 growth forecast to be restated - TV.
newsitem.headline: Singapore 1996 growth forecast to be restated - TV.

text.p: Singapore will announce a new forecast for the country's economic growth in 1996 in mid-November, state television on Wednesday quoted Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong as saying.
It also quoted Yeo as saying Singapore's fourth quarter growth figures would be fairly weak, but the extent would only be known in the next two weeks.
State television, which reported the comments on its text news service, did not give a context for Yeo's remarks.
Singapore's most recent official growth forecast, repeated by Yeo as recently as September 24, was that the economy would grow by "seven to eight percent" in 1996.
But the city-state has been hurt in recent months by a global slump in demand for electronic products, on which it is heavily dependent.
Electronics, computers and related products account for about 50 percent of Singapore's total industrial production and almost 60 percent of its non-oil exports.

A Reuters poll on Tuesday forecast Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) would grow by only 6.4 percent this year. A similar poll last week forecast a rise of 6.5 percent and a previous poll in September forecast growth at 7.1 percent.
The new poll followed the announcement on Monday of a surprise 6.2 percent fall in the island's non-oil domestic exports in September.

Most economists now expect Singapore's GDP growth in the third quarter of this year to average slightly over 3.0 percent year-on-year. Growth in the fourth quarter is expected to average around 4.9 percent.
